$comment: API docs written by Claude (AI) from the Nucleus and Proto Input source, for members the official docs (splitscreen.me) and the source comments leave out. Each says what it is based on; the tools show it as written by Claude. Human docs take priority unless "override" is set (where the official text is wrong). Edit freely; a person who reviews one can drop it here and add it to the official docs instead.

Game.Play.doc: Called once per instance (player), in player order. By default it runs after Nucleus has set up the instance (Goldberg, XInput DLLs, ...) and before the game starts, and `Context.StartArguments` is read after it. `Game.GamePlayBeforeGameSetup` runs it before that setup; `Game.GamePlayAfterLaunch` runs it after the game has started (then `Context.StartArguments` has no effect). If both are true it never runs. `Context`, `Player`, `PlayerList`, `Handler` and `ProtoInput` are available inside it. An error thrown here ends the whole session.

Game.GamePlayAfterLaunch.doc: Run `Game.Play` after the instance has been launched instead of before. Changes to `Context.StartArguments` then have no effect. Don't combine with `Game.GamePlayBeforeGameSetup`: if both are true, `Game.Play` never runs.

Game.GamePlayBeforeGameSetup.doc: Run `Game.Play` before the majority of the instance is set up (Goldberg, XInput DLLs, ...) instead of after it. Don't combine with `Game.GamePlayAfterLaunch`: if both are true, `Game.Play` never runs.

Game.OnStop.doc: Called when the session ends, with the last player's `Context`/`Player`. If it throws, Nucleus skips its cleanup (leftover processes, registry restore, temporary users, backups), so keep it error-free. `Context` is undefined if the session ends before the first instance was set up.

Game.OnFinishedSetup.doc: Called once after all instances have been set up and started, with the last player's `Context`/`Player`. An error thrown here ends the session.

Game.SetupSse.doc: Never called by Nucleus (declared but unused): assigning it has no effect.

Game.AddOption.doc: Adds a user-selectable option to the game profile. Read it back in `Game.Play` with `Context.Options["key"]`.

Game.ShowOptionAsStep.doc: Shows a previously added option as its own setup step before launching.

Game.Hub.doc: Hub metadata. Written by hub.splitscreen.me when the handler is uploaded, and kept up to date there. Don't add or edit these lines yourself.

Game.Hook.doc: Settings for Nucleus' custom xinput/x360ce hook DLL.

Game.ProtoInput.doc: Proto Input options (multiple mice/keyboards, focus hooks, input redirection). See https://www.splitscreen.me/docs/protoinput

Game.OnCustomHotKey_1.doc: Called when the first custom hotkey from `Game.CustomHotkeys` is pressed. Required if that hotkey is defined (Nucleus calls it without checking). `Context` is the last player's, or undefined before the first instance is set up.

Game.OnCustomHotKey_2.doc: Called when the second custom hotkey from `Game.CustomHotkeys` is pressed. Required if that hotkey is defined (Nucleus calls it without checking). `Context` is the last player's, or undefined before the first instance is set up.

Game.OnCustomHotKey_3.doc: Called when the third custom hotkey from `Game.CustomHotkeys` is pressed. Required if that hotkey is defined (Nucleus calls it without checking). `Context` is the last player's, or undefined before the first instance is set up.

Game.ExecutableNames.doc: Alternative executable names this handler matches (e.g. different store versions).

Game.Debug.doc: Writes a detailed debug log while the handler runs.

Context.Width.doc: Width in pixels of this instance's window.

Context.Height.doc: Height in pixels of this instance's window.

Context.PosX.doc: X position of this instance's window.

Context.PosY.doc: Y position of this instance's window.

Context.MonitorWidth.doc: Width of the monitor this instance is on.

Context.MonitorHeight.doc: Height of the monitor this instance is on.

Context.PlayerID.doc: Zero-based index of the player/instance being set up.

Context.NumberOfPlayers.doc: Total number of players in this session.

Context.PlayerSteamID.doc: Steam ID assigned to the current player.

Context.HasKeyboardPlayer.doc: True if any player in the session uses keyboard & mouse.

Context.RootFolder.doc: Root of the current instance's game folder (Nucleus-Coop\content\<GUID>\Instance<N>).

Context.ExePath.doc: Full path of the executable being launched for this instance.

Context.Options.doc: Values chosen by the user for options added with `Game.AddOption`.

Context.Arch.doc: Architecture of the game executable ("x86" or "x64").

Context.ModifySaveFile.doc: Edits keys in an INI/CFG file. Example: `Context.ModifySaveFile(path, path, Nucleus.SaveType.INI, [new Nucleus.IniSaveInfo("Section", "Key", "Value")]);`

Context.PatchFile.doc: Patches bytes in a file (copy of the original). The file must be excluded from symlinking (e.g. via `Game.FileSymlinkExclusions`).

Context.StartProcess.doc: Starts a process with arguments, optionally elevated.

Context.Wait.doc: Pauses the handler for the given number of milliseconds.

Context.Log.doc: Writes a line to the Nucleus debug log (requires `Game.Debug = true` or debug logging enabled).

Context.RandomInt.doc: Returns a random integer between min and max.

Context.RandomString.doc: Returns a random alphanumeric string of the given length.

Context.HexEdit.doc: Writes bytes at an address in a file.

Context.CopyScriptFolder.doc: Copies the handler's folder (Game.Folder) to the given destination.

Context.CustomUserPlayerValues.doc: Answers to `Game.CustomUserPlayerPrompts` for the current player.

Context.CustomUserInstanceValues.doc: Answers to `Game.CustomUserInstancePrompts` for the current instance.

Player.ProtoInputInstanceHandle.doc: Proto Input's handle for this player's game instance. Nucleus sets it when Proto Input injects into the instance (at launch with `Game.ProtoInput.InjectStartup`, or after launch with a runtime injection); it is 0 before that and when Proto Input isn't used. Inside `Game.Play` it is usually still 0, since Proto Input injects after it; use it in callbacks such as `Game.ProtoInput.OnInputLocked`.
Player.ProtoInputInstanceHandle.basis: Nucleus PlayerInfo.cs, ProtoInputLauncher.cs (SetupInstance, InjectStartup, InjectRuntime), GenericGameHandler.cs (call order)

Player.IsXInput.doc: True if this player's gamepad was detected through XInput on the setup screen (done when `Game.Hook.XInputEnabled` is on without `XInputReroute` and `Game.ProtoInput.DinputDeviceHook`, or with `Game.ProtoInput.XinputHook`). False for DirectInput, SDL2 and keyboard/mouse players.
Player.IsXInput.basis: Nucleus PlayerInfo.cs (IsXInput setter), DevicesFunctions.cs (gamepad polling), GameProfile.cs (profile load)

Context.CopyFolder.doc: Copies the folder `source` with all its files and subfolders into `destination` (both full paths), creating the destination folders. Files that already exist at the destination are not overwritten, and files that fail to copy are skipped silently. Throws if `source` doesn't exist; returns true.

Context.SteamLang.doc: The Steam language name for the game, for example `english`. Nucleus takes the game's own Steam language setting in Nucleus, else Nucleus's global Steam language setting, else the Steam client's language from the registry, and `english` if that is empty. `Game.GoldbergLanguage`, when set, overrides all of these.

Player.ProtoController1.doc: First controller index Proto Input gives this player's instance: one-based (1 is the first gamepad, i.e. `GamepadId + 1`), 0 means none. Nucleus sets it for each player right after `Game.Play`, overwriting your value, unless `Game.UseManualProtoControllersSetup` is true. It is only sent to Proto Input when `Game.ProtoInput.MultipleProtoControllers` is true; otherwise Nucleus sends `GamepadId + 1` (0 for raw mouse/keyboard players).

Context.OrigRootFolder.doc: The original game folder: the folder of the game executable the user picked, in lower case, with `Game.BinariesFolder` removed. Set per player when the instance is set up, before `Game.Play`. `Context.RootFolder` is the instance's own folder.
Context.OrigRootFolder.basis: Nucleus GenericGameHandler.cs (rootFolder from exeFolder.ToLower() and BinariesFolder; context.OrigRootFolder = rootFolder)

Player.ProtoController2.doc: Second controller index Proto Input gives this player's instance: one-based, 0 means none. With `Game.ProtoInput.MultipleProtoControllers`, Nucleus sets it right after `Game.Play` to the first guest's `GamepadId + 1`, or to the player's own if there are no guests (otherwise 0), unless `Game.UseManualProtoControllersSetup` is true. Only sent to Proto Input when `MultipleProtoControllers` is true.

Player.ProtoController3.doc: Third controller index Proto Input gives this player's instance: one-based, 0 means none. With `Game.ProtoInput.MultipleProtoControllers`, Nucleus sets it right after `Game.Play` to the second guest's `GamepadId + 1`, or to the player's own if there are no guests (otherwise 0), unless `Game.UseManualProtoControllersSetup` is true. Only sent to Proto Input when `MultipleProtoControllers` is true.

Player.ProtoController4.doc: Fourth controller index Proto Input gives this player's instance: one-based, 0 means none. With `Game.ProtoInput.MultipleProtoControllers`, Nucleus sets it right after `Game.Play` to the third guest's `GamepadId + 1`, or to the player's own if there are no guests (otherwise 0), unless `Game.UseManualProtoControllersSetup` is true. Only sent to Proto Input when `MultipleProtoControllers` is true.

Context.PatchFileFindPattern.doc: Reads `originalFile`, replaces every occurrence of the hex byte pattern `origPattern` (spaces allowed) and writes the result to `patchedFile`, even if nothing matched. Two forms: (`originalFile`, `patchedFile`, `origPattern`, `patchPattern`, `patchall`) puts the hex `patchPattern` in place of each match; (`originalFile`, `patchedFile`, `origPattern`, `insert`, `offset`, `patchall`) writes the low two bytes of the number `insert` (little-endian) into the pattern at one-based byte position `offset`. Throws if `originalFile` doesn't exist; returns true. In the first form, `patchall` false patches only the first byte of each match: pass true.

Player.IsKeyboardPlayer.doc: True for a keyboard/mouse player: the single shared keyboard player Nucleus adds on the setup screen when `Game.SupportsKeyboard` is true, and every player using a raw mouse or keyboard device. False for gamepad players.
Player.IsKeyboardPlayer.basis: Nucleus PlayerInfo.cs (IsKeyboardPlayer setter), DevicesFunctions.cs (kbPlayer, GamepadId 99), RawInputManager.cs, GameProfile.cs (profile load)

Context.BackupFile.doc: Copies a file to `<name>_NUCLEUS_BACKUP<ext>` next to it; when the session ends Nucleus deletes the original and moves the backup back. Parameters: the full path (or an array of paths), then `overwrite`, whether to replace an existing backup (false throws if one exists). The single-path form only acts for the first player (`PlayerID` 0); the array form acts for every player. A missing file is skipped with a log line; returns true.
Context.BackupFile.basis: Nucleus GenericContext.cs (BackupFile, both overloads), GenericGameHandler.cs (userBackedFiles restore on end)

Context.ChangeXmlAttributeValue.doc: Opens the XML file `path` (environment variables like `%APPDATA%` are expanded), sets attribute `attributeName` to `attributeValue` on every node matching the XPath `xpath`, and saves the file. Throws if the file doesn't exist or a matching node lacks that attribute (it doesn't create attributes); returns true.

Context.NumControllers.doc: Number of players in the session that are not keyboard players (`IsKeyboardPlayer` false). Nucleus only counts it in the first player's Context, before `Game.Play`; in every other player's Context it is 0. `Context.NumKeyboards` counts the keyboard players.
Context.NumControllers.basis: Nucleus GenericContext.cs, GenericGameHandler.cs (counting loop under if (i == 0) after CreateContext)

Player.Owner.doc: The setup-screen screen (a `UserScreen`) this player was placed on, with members such as `MonitorBounds`, `DisplayIndex` and `Type`. Nucleus sets it when the player is dropped onto a screen or loaded from a saved profile, and clears it to null when the player is removed from the screen.
Player.Owner.basis: Nucleus PlayerInfo.cs, UserScreen.cs, BoundsFunctions.cs (player.Owner = Screens[screenIndex] / null), GameProfile.cs (SetProfilePlayerDatas)

Game.HookReRegisterRawInputMouse.doc: Includes the mouse when the Nucleus hook re-registers the game window's raw input so it keeps receiving input in the background. Only read when `Game.HookReRegisterRawInput` is on and the Nucleus hook DLL is injected (`Game.HookFocus`, `Game.SetWindowHook`, `Game.HideCursor`, `Game.PreventWindowDeactivation` or `Game.SupportsMultipleKeyboardsAndMice`). Default `true`; `false` leaves the game's mouse registration as it is.
Game.HookReRegisterRawInputMouse.basis: Nucleus DllsInjector.cs (InjectDLLs), GenericGameHandler.cs (InjectDLLs call sites), Nucleus.Inject Program.cs, Nucleus.Hook Hook.cpp + RawInputReRegister.cpp (reRegisterRawInput)

Game.HookReRegisterRawInputKeyboard.doc: Includes the keyboard when the Nucleus hook re-registers the game window's raw input so it keeps receiving input in the background. Only read when `Game.HookReRegisterRawInput` is on and the Nucleus hook DLL is injected (`Game.HookFocus`, `Game.SetWindowHook`, `Game.HideCursor`, `Game.PreventWindowDeactivation` or `Game.SupportsMultipleKeyboardsAndMice`). Default `true`; `false` leaves the game's keyboard registration as it is.
Game.HookReRegisterRawInputKeyboard.basis: Nucleus DllsInjector.cs (InjectDLLs), GenericGameHandler.cs (InjectDLLs call sites), Nucleus.Inject Program.cs, Nucleus.Hook Hook.cpp + RawInputReRegister.cpp (reRegisterRawInput)

Game.ProtoInput.InjectRuntime_EasyHookMe.doc: Injects Proto Input with EasyHook into each instance's running game once Nucleus has found its process, then applies the `Game.ProtoInput` options. Ignored when `Game.ProtoInput.InjectStartup` is on, and `Game.ProtoInput.InjectRuntime_EasyHookStealthMethod` takes priority over it. If injection fails, Nucleus shows an error and ends the session.
Game.ProtoInput.InjectRuntime_EasyHookMe.basis: Nucleus GenericGameHandler.cs (StartGame, runtime inject block), ProtoInputLauncher.cs (InjectRuntime, SetupInstance); ProtoInputLoader EasyHookRuntime.cpp

Game.ProtoInput.InjectStartup.doc: Nucleus starts each instance's game suspended, injects Proto Input, applies the `Game.ProtoInput` options and only then lets the game run, so the hooks are in place from its first line of code. This replaces Nucleus's other launch methods and the `InjectRuntime_…` options; it is not used with `Game.ThirdPartyLaunch` or `Game.NeedsSteamEmulation`. If injection fails, Nucleus shows an error and ends the session.
Game.ProtoInput.InjectStartup.basis: Nucleus GenericGameHandler.cs (StartGame launch branch, runtime inject condition), ProtoInputLauncher.cs (InjectStartup, SetupInstance); ProtoInputLoader EasyHookStartup.cpp (RtlCreateSuspendedProcess)

Game.ProtoInput.InjectRuntime_RemoteLoad.doc: Injects Proto Input into each instance's running game by making the game load the Proto Input DLL itself (a remote LoadLibrary call), once Nucleus has found its process, then applies the `Game.ProtoInput` options. Ignored when `Game.ProtoInput.InjectStartup`, `Game.ProtoInput.InjectRuntime_EasyHookMethod` or `Game.ProtoInput.InjectRuntime_EasyHookStealthMethod` is on. If injection fails, Nucleus shows an error and ends the session.
Game.ProtoInput.InjectRuntime_RemoteLoad.basis: Nucleus GenericGameHandler.cs (StartGame, runtime inject block), ProtoInputLauncher.cs (InjectRuntime priority order); ProtoInputLoader RemoteLoadLibrary.cpp

Game.LockInputSuspendsExplorer.doc: Pauses the Windows Explorer threads behind the taskbar, Start menu and Alt+Tab while input is locked, so they can't react to input; they resume when input is unlocked. Read on every lock (the lock key, the gamepad lock shortcut or `Game.LockInputAtStart`). Default `false`.
Game.LockInputSuspendsExplorer.basis: Nucleus LockInputRuntime.cs (Lock/Unlock), RawInputProcessor.cs, GamepadShortcuts.cs, GenericGameHandler.cs (LockInputAtStart); ProtoInputUtil KillExplorer.cpp (SuspendExplorer/RestartExplorer)

Game.ProtoInput.SendMouseWheelMessages.doc: Proto Input turns the player's mouse wheel into mouse wheel window messages sent to the game window. Applied per instance when Proto Input is injected (`Game.ProtoInput.InjectStartup` or an `InjectRuntime_…` option). Not sent while `Game.ProtoInput.TranslateMKBtoXinput` is on.
Game.ProtoInput.SendMouseWheelMessages.basis: Nucleus ProtoInputLauncher.cs (SetupInstance → SetupMessagesToSend); ProtoInputHooks PipeCommunication.cpp, RawInput.cpp (SendInputMessages, ProcessMouseInput)

Game.ProtoInput.SendMouseButtonMessages.doc: Proto Input turns the player's mouse clicks (left, right, middle and the two side buttons) into button down/up window messages sent to the game window. Applied per instance when Proto Input is injected (`Game.ProtoInput.InjectStartup` or an `InjectRuntime_…` option). Ignored when `Game.ProtoInput.SendMouseDblClkMessages` is on (that option sends the clicks itself) or `Game.ProtoInput.TranslateMKBtoXinput` is on.

Game.ProtoInput.SendMouseMovementMessage.doc: Proto Input sends a mouse move window message with the player's fake cursor position to the game window each time the player's mouse moves. Applied per instance when Proto Input is injected (`Game.ProtoInput.InjectStartup` or an `InjectRuntime_…` option). Not sent while `Game.ProtoInput.TranslateMKBtoXinput` is on.
Game.ProtoInput.SendMouseMovementMessage.basis: Nucleus ProtoInputLauncher.cs (SetupInstance → SetupMessagesToSend); ProtoInputHooks RawInput.cpp (SendInputMessages, ProcessMouseInput)

Game.ProtoInput.RenameHandlesHook.doc: Gives each instance its own copy of the named mutexes, events and semaphores listed in `Game.ProtoInput.RenameHandles` (and named pipes in `Game.ProtoInput.RenameNamedPipes`) by adding a random number to any name that contains a listed text, so instances don't detect each other. Only affects names the game creates or opens after Proto Input is injected. Needs `Game.ProtoInput.InjectStartup` or an `InjectRuntime_…` option.
Game.ProtoInput.RenameHandlesHook.basis: Nucleus ProtoInputLauncher.cs (SetupInstance: InstallHook RenameHandlesHookID, AddHandleToRename, AddNamedPipeToRename); ProtoInputHooks RenameHandlesHook.cpp (updateName, Nt* hooks)

Game.ProtoInput.OnInputLocked.doc: Function Nucleus calls each time input is locked (the lock key, the gamepad lock shortcut or `Game.LockInputAtStart`), and once after all instances are set up if input is locked by then. It sees the last player's `Context`.
Game.ProtoInput.OnInputLocked.basis: Nucleus LockInputRuntime.cs (Lock), GenericGameHandler.cs (after instance loop); AGENTS.md (last player's Context)

Game.ProtoInput.OnInputUnlocked.doc: Function Nucleus calls each time input is unlocked, once after all instances are set up if input is not locked by then, and when the session ends (before `Game.OnStop`). It sees the last player's `Context`.
Game.ProtoInput.OnInputUnlocked.basis: Nucleus LockInputRuntime.cs (Unlock), GenericGameHandler.cs (after instance loop; End)

Game.SendFakeFocusMsg.doc: Sends focus messages once to every player's game window, one second apart, after the last instance has started, to make each game believe it has focus. `Game.FakeFocusSendActivate` adds the activate message. Not run with `Game.ProcessChangesAtEnd`.

Game.ProtoInput.EnableToggleFakeCursorVi.doc: Lets the player show or hide Proto Input's fake cursor with a key on their own keyboard (`Game.ProtoInput.ToggleFakeCursorVisibilityShortcutVkey`, Home by default); that key press is not passed to the game as a message. Needs `Game.ProtoInput.InjectStartup` or an `InjectRuntime_…` option.
Game.ProtoInput.EnableToggleFakeCursorVi.basis: Nucleus ProtoInputLauncher.cs (SetupInstance → SetToggleFakeCursorVisibilityShortcut), ProtoInputOptions.cs (Vkey default 0x24); ProtoInputHooks RawInput.cpp (SendKeyMessage)

Game.ProtoInput.FocusLoopIntervalMillise.doc: Milliseconds Proto Input's focus loop waits between rounds of focus messages to the game window. Default `5`. Only read when `Game.ProtoInput.EnableFocusMessageLoop` is on and Proto Input is injected (`Game.ProtoInput.InjectStartup` or an `InjectRuntime_…` option).
Game.ProtoInput.FocusLoopIntervalMillise.basis: Nucleus ProtoInputLauncher.cs (SetupInstance → StartFocusMessageLoop), ProtoInputOptions.cs; ProtoInputHooks FocusMessageLoop.cpp (LoopThread)

Game.ProtoInput.FocusLoop_WM_ACTIVATE.doc: Proto Input's focus loop repeatedly tells the game window it was activated by a click (WM_ACTIVATE), so it believes it still has focus. Only read when `Game.ProtoInput.EnableFocusMessageLoop` is on and Proto Input is injected (`Game.ProtoInput.InjectStartup` or an `InjectRuntime_…` option).

Game.ProtoInput.FocusLoop_WM_ACTIVATEAPP.doc: Proto Input's focus loop repeatedly tells the game that its app became the active one (WM_ACTIVATEAPP), so it believes it still has focus. Only read when `Game.ProtoInput.EnableFocusMessageLoop` is on and Proto Input is injected (`Game.ProtoInput.InjectStartup` or an `InjectRuntime_…` option).

Game.ProtoInput.FocusLoop_WM_NCACTIVATE.doc: Proto Input's focus loop repeatedly tells the game window to show itself as active (WM_NCACTIVATE), so it believes it still has focus. Only read when `Game.ProtoInput.EnableFocusMessageLoop` is on and Proto Input is injected (`Game.ProtoInput.InjectStartup` or an `InjectRuntime_…` option).

Game.ProtoInput.FocusLoop_WM_MOUSEACTIVA.doc: Proto Input's focus loop repeatedly tells the game window it is being activated by the mouse (WM_MOUSEACTIVATE). Only read when `Game.ProtoInput.EnableFocusMessageLoop` is on and Proto Input is injected (`Game.ProtoInput.InjectStartup` or an `InjectRuntime_…` option).

Game.ProtoInput.FocusLoop_WM_SETFOCUS.doc: Proto Input's focus loop repeatedly tells the game window it has keyboard focus (WM_SETFOCUS). Only read when `Game.ProtoInput.EnableFocusMessageLoop` is on and Proto Input is injected (`Game.ProtoInput.InjectStartup` or an `InjectRuntime_…` option).

Game.IgnoreWindowBorderCheck.doc: Skips the window pass Nucleus runs after the last instance has started and when windows are reset: it re-applies position, size and border removal to game windows that still have a border, and applies `Game.WindowStyleEndChanges`, `Game.ExtWindowStyleEndChanges` and `Game.EnableWindows`. Default `false`.
Game.IgnoreWindowBorderCheck.basis: Nucleus GenericGameHandler.cs (last-instance block), GlobalWindowMethods.cs (RemoveBorder, reset-windows update loop, ResetWindows)

Game.ProtoInput.AutoHideTaskbar.doc: Turns on the Windows taskbar's auto-hide when the session starts and turns it off again when the session ends. Does nothing if auto-hide was already on, or when `Game.HideTaskbar` hides the taskbar instead. Works without Proto Input being injected.

ProtoInput.EnableMessageFilter.doc: Turns on a window message filter in the game instance. Parameters: the instance handle (`Player.ProtoInputInstanceHandle`) and a filter ID from `ProtoInput.Values` (the `...FilterID` values). Filters only act while the `MessageFilterHookID` hook is installed.
ProtoInput.EnableMessageFilter.basis: Nucleus ProtoInput.cs (EnableMessageFilter), ProtoInputLoader InstallMessageFilter.cpp, ProtoInputHooks PipeCommunication.cpp (SetupMessageFilter), ProtoInputHooks MessageFilterHook.cpp (FilterMessage)

ProtoInput.DisableMessageFilter.doc: Turns off a window message filter in the game instance. Parameters: the instance handle (`Player.ProtoInputInstanceHandle`) and a filter ID from `ProtoInput.Values` (the `...FilterID` values).
ProtoInput.DisableMessageFilter.basis: Nucleus ProtoInput.cs (DisableMessageFilter), ProtoInputLoader InstallMessageFilter.cpp, ProtoInputHooks MessageFilterHook.cpp (SetFilterEnabled)

ProtoInput.Values.MouseButtonFilterID.doc: Selects the mouse button filter (ID 6): only mouse button messages synthesized by Proto Input reach the game, so the real mouse doesn't interfere. Only acts while `MessageFilterHookID` is installed. Pass it to `ProtoInput.EnableMessageFilter` or `ProtoInput.DisableMessageFilter`.
ProtoInput.Values.MouseButtonFilterID.basis: Nucleus ProtoInput.cs (ExposedValues, ProtoMessageFilterIDs), ProtoInputHooks MouseButtonFilter.h, ProtoInputHooks MessageFilterHook.cpp (FilterMessage)

ProtoInput.InstallHook.doc: Installs a Proto Input hook in the game instance. Parameters: the instance handle (`Player.ProtoInputInstanceHandle`) and a hook ID from `ProtoInput.Values` (the `...HookID` values). An unknown handle does nothing, and the call waits until Proto Input in the game has connected.
ProtoInput.InstallHook.basis: Nucleus ProtoInput.cs (InstallHook), ProtoInputLoader InstallHooks.cpp + InstanceHandling.cpp (WaitClientConnect), ProtoInputHooks HookManager.cpp (InstallHook)

ProtoInput.UninstallHook.doc: Removes a Proto Input hook from the game instance. Parameters: the instance handle (`Player.ProtoInputInstanceHandle`) and a hook ID from `ProtoInput.Values` (the `...HookID` values).
ProtoInput.UninstallHook.basis: Nucleus ProtoInput.cs (UninstallHook), ProtoInputLoader InstallHooks.cpp, ProtoInputHooks HookManager.cpp (UninstallHook)

ProtoInput.Values.RawInputFilterID.doc: Selects the raw input filter (ID 0): `WM_INPUT` messages always say they arrived while the game was in the foreground. Only acts while `MessageFilterHookID` is installed. Pass it to `ProtoInput.EnableMessageFilter` or `ProtoInput.DisableMessageFilter`.
ProtoInput.Values.RawInputFilterID.basis: Nucleus ProtoInput.cs (ExposedValues, ProtoMessageFilterIDs), ProtoInputHooks RawInputFilter.h, ProtoInputHooks MessageFilterHook.cpp (FilterMessage)

ProtoInput.Values.MouseWheelFilterID.doc: Selects the mouse wheel filter (ID 5): only `WM_MOUSEWHEEL` messages synthesized by Proto Input reach the game, so scrolling isn't sent twice. Only acts while `MessageFilterHookID` is installed. Pass it to `ProtoInput.EnableMessageFilter` or `ProtoInput.DisableMessageFilter`.
ProtoInput.Values.MouseWheelFilterID.basis: Nucleus ProtoInput.cs (ExposedValues, ProtoMessageFilterIDs), ProtoInputHooks MouseWheelFilter.h, ProtoInputHooks MessageFilterHook.cpp (FilterMessage)

ProtoInput.Values.GetCursorPosHookID.doc: Selects the GetCursorPos hook (ID 3): gives each instance its own cursor position, as `GetCursorPos` returns the instance's fake cursor. Pass it to `ProtoInput.InstallHook` or `ProtoInput.UninstallHook`.

ProtoInput.Values.SetCursorPosHookID.doc: Selects the SetCursorPos hook (ID 4): the game's `SetCursorPos` moves only the instance's fake cursor, not the real one. Pass it to `ProtoInput.InstallHook` or `ProtoInput.UninstallHook`.

ProtoInput.Values.CursorVisibilityStateH.doc: Selects the cursor visibility hook (ID 8): the game's `ShowCursor`, `SetCursor` and `SetSystemCursor` calls show, hide and set the image of the instance's fake cursor. Pass it to `ProtoInput.InstallHook` or `ProtoInput.UninstallHook`.
ProtoInput.Values.CursorVisibilityStateH.basis: Nucleus ProtoInput.cs (ExposedValues, ProtoHookIDs), ProtoInputHooks CursorVisibilityHook.cpp (Hook_ShowCursor, Hook_SetCursor, Hook_SetSystemCursor)

ProtoInput.SetDrawFakeCursor.doc: Shows or hides the fake cursor Proto Input draws over the game for this instance. Parameters: the instance handle and `true`/`false`.
ProtoInput.SetDrawFakeCursor.basis: Nucleus ProtoInput.cs (SetDrawFakeCursor), ProtoInputLoader Inject.cpp, ProtoInputHooks PipeCommunication.cpp (SetDrawFakeCursor), ProtoInputHooks FakeCursor.cpp (EnableDisableFakeCursor)

ProtoInput.Values.GetKeyStateHookID.doc: Selects the GetKeyState hook (ID 5): `GetKeyState` reports the keys and buttons of the instance's assigned keyboard and mouse. Pass it to `ProtoInput.InstallHook` or `ProtoInput.UninstallHook`.

ProtoInput.Values.GetAsyncKeyStateHookID.doc: Selects the GetAsyncKeyState hook (ID 6): `GetAsyncKeyState` reports the keys and buttons of the instance's assigned keyboard and mouse. Pass it to `ProtoInput.InstallHook` or `ProtoInput.UninstallHook`.

ProtoInput.Values.GetKeyboardStateHookID.doc: Selects the GetKeyboardState hook (ID 7): `GetKeyboardState` reports the keys and buttons of the instance's assigned keyboard and mouse. Pass it to `ProtoInput.InstallHook` or `ProtoInput.UninstallHook`.

ProtoInput.Values.MouseActivateFilterID.doc: Selects the mouse activate filter (ID 2): `WM_MOUSEACTIVATE` messages always tell the game it is being focused. Only acts while `MessageFilterHookID` is installed. Pass it to `ProtoInput.EnableMessageFilter` or `ProtoInput.DisableMessageFilter`.
ProtoInput.Values.MouseActivateFilterID.basis: Nucleus ProtoInput.cs (ExposedValues, ProtoMessageFilterIDs), ProtoInputHooks MouseActivateFilter.h, ProtoInputHooks MessageFilterHook.cpp (FilterMessage)

ProtoInput.Values.WindowActivateFilterID.doc: Selects the window activate filter (ID 3): `WM_ACTIVATE` messages always say the game window is active. Only acts while `MessageFilterHookID` is installed. Pass it to `ProtoInput.EnableMessageFilter` or `ProtoInput.DisableMessageFilter`.
ProtoInput.Values.WindowActivateFilterID.basis: Nucleus ProtoInput.cs (ExposedValues, ProtoMessageFilterIDs), ProtoInputHooks WindowActivateFilter.h, ProtoInputHooks MessageFilterHook.cpp (FilterMessage)

ProtoInput.Values.MouseMoveFilterID.doc: Selects the mouse move filter (ID 1): `WM_MOUSEMOVE` messages carry the instance's fake cursor position and button and modifier state. Only acts while `MessageFilterHookID` is installed. Pass it to `ProtoInput.EnableMessageFilter` or `ProtoInput.DisableMessageFilter`.
ProtoInput.Values.MouseMoveFilterID.basis: Nucleus ProtoInput.cs (ExposedValues, ProtoMessageFilterIDs), ProtoInputHooks MouseMoveFilter.h, ProtoInputHooks MessageFilterHook.cpp (FilterMessage)

ProtoInput.SetManualScaling.basis: Nucleus ProtoInput.cs (SetManualScaling), ProtoInputLoader Inject.cpp, ProtoInputHooks PipeCommunication.cpp, ProtoInputHooks WindowMsgHook.cpp (Settings, getfactor), Nucleus ProtoInputLauncher.cs

ProtoInput.SetXinputtoMKBkeys.doc: Sets the controller-to-keyboard mapping used by `ProtoInput.SetTranslateXinputtoMKB`. Parameters, in order: the instance handle; virtual-key codes for A, B, X, Y, right shoulder, left shoulder, D-pad right, left, up, down, right stick press, left stick press, stick right, left, up, down, Back and Start; then sensitivity, acceleration and deadzone.
ProtoInput.SetXinputtoMKBkeys.basis: Nucleus ProtoInput.cs (SetXinputtoMKBkeys), ProtoInputLoader Inject.cpp, ProtoInputHooks PipeCommunication.cpp (SetXinputtoMKBkeys), ProtoInputHooks TranslateXtoMKB.cpp (ButtonStateImpulse, Sens, Sensmult, Deadzone), Nucleus ProtoInputLauncher.cs (defaults)

ProtoInput.SetXinputtoMKBCFG.doc: Sets options for `ProtoInput.SetTranslateXinputtoMKB`. Parameters, in order: the instance handle; swap sticks; screen scanning (moves the cursor to points found from .bmp images or static points); shoulder buttons jump to the next point; then for A, B, X and Y in turn: static point, click, move.
ProtoInput.SetXinputtoMKBCFG.basis: Nucleus ProtoInput.cs (SetXinputtoMKBCFG), ProtoInputLoader Inject.cpp, ProtoInputHooks PipeCommunication.cpp (SetXinputtoMKBCFG, scanAtype...), ProtoInputHooks ScanThread.cpp, TranslateXtoMKB.cpp (lefthanded)

ProtoInput.Values.ClipCursorHookID.doc: Selects the ClipCursor hook (ID 9): the game's `ClipCursor` no longer confines the real cursor; by default it confines the fake cursor instead (see `ProtoInput.SetCursorClipOptions`). Pass it to `ProtoInput.InstallHook` or `ProtoInput.UninstallHook`.
ProtoInput.Values.ClipCursorHookID.basis: Nucleus ProtoInput.cs (ExposedValues, ProtoHookIDs), ProtoInputHooks ClipCursorHook.cpp (Hook_ClipCursor, Hook_GetClipCursor)

ProtoInput.Values.RenameHandlesHookID.doc: Selects the rename handles hook (ID 11): mutexes, events, semaphores and named pipes whose names match `ProtoInput.AddHandleToRename` or `ProtoInput.AddNamedPipeToRename` get a unique name, so instances don't block each other. Pass it to `ProtoInput.InstallHook` or `ProtoInput.UninstallHook`.
ProtoInput.Values.RenameHandlesHookID.basis: Nucleus ProtoInput.cs (ExposedValues, ProtoHookIDs), ProtoInputHooks RenameHandlesHook.cpp (updateName, InstallImpl)

ProtoInput.Values.XinputHookID.doc: Selects the XInput hook (ID 12): each instance sees only the controllers chosen by `ProtoInput.SetControllerIndex`, in the order given. Pass it to `ProtoInput.InstallHook` or `ProtoInput.UninstallHook`.
ProtoInput.Values.XinputHookID.basis: Nucleus ProtoInput.cs (ExposedValues, ProtoHookIDs), ProtoInputHooks XinputHook.cpp (Hook_XInputGetState, GetTargetControllerIndex, InstallImpl)

ProtoInput.Values.DinputOrderHookID.doc: Selects the DirectInput order hook (ID 13): every DirectInput device the game creates opens the controller set by `ProtoInput.SetDinputDeviceGUID`; without one set, DirectInput devices fail to open. Pass it to `ProtoInput.InstallHook` or `ProtoInput.UninstallHook`.
ProtoInput.Values.DinputOrderHookID.basis: Nucleus ProtoInput.cs (ExposedValues, ProtoHookIDs), ProtoInputHooks DinputOrderHook.cpp (Hook_DinputCreateDevice8W, blockDinput)

ProtoInput.Values.SetWindowPosHookID.doc: Selects the SetWindowPos hook (ID 14): every `SetWindowPos` call uses the position and size from `ProtoInput.SetSetWindowPosSettings`. Pass it to `ProtoInput.InstallHook` or `ProtoInput.UninstallHook`.

ProtoInput.Values.BlockRawInputHookID.doc: Selects the block raw input hook (ID 15): `GetRawInputDeviceList` and `GetRegisteredRawInputDevices` report no devices to the game. Pass it to `ProtoInput.InstallHook` or `ProtoInput.UninstallHook`.

ProtoInput.Values.FindWindowHookID.doc: Selects the FindWindow hook (ID 16): `FindWindow` and `FindWindowEx` find nothing and `EnumWindows` lists no windows, so an instance can't find another instance's window. Pass it to `ProtoInput.InstallHook` or `ProtoInput.UninstallHook`.

ProtoInput.Values.CreateSingleHIDHookID.doc: Selects the single HID hook (ID 17): once `ProtoInput.SetCreateSingleHIDName` is set, the game can open only that HID device path. Pass it to `ProtoInput.InstallHook` or `ProtoInput.UninstallHook`.
ProtoInput.Values.CreateSingleHIDHookID.basis: Nucleus ProtoInput.cs (ExposedValues, ProtoHookIDs), ProtoInputHooks CreateSingleHIDHook.cpp (Hook_CreateFileW, SetRawHidW)

ProtoInput.Values.WindowStyleHookID.doc: Selects the window style hook (ID 18): window styles the game sets with `SetWindowLong`/`SetWindowLongPtr` lose the border, system menu and dialog frame. Pass it to `ProtoInput.InstallHook` or `ProtoInput.UninstallHook`.

ProtoInput.Values.MoveWindowHookID.doc: Selects the MoveWindow hook (ID 19): every `MoveWindow` call uses the position and size from `ProtoInput.SetMoveWindowSettings`. Pass it to `ProtoInput.InstallHook` or `ProtoInput.UninstallHook`.

ProtoInput.Values.AdjustWindowRectHookID.doc: Selects the AdjustWindowRect hook (ID 20): `AdjustWindowRect` and `AdjustWindowRectEx` compute the window size from the rectangle set by `ProtoInput.SetAdjustWindowRectSettings`. Pass it to `ProtoInput.InstallHook` or `ProtoInput.UninstallHook`.

ProtoInput.Values.RemoveBorderHookID.doc: Selects the remove border hook (ID 21): removes the main window's border and title bar on install (see `ProtoInput.SetDontWaitWindowBorder`), and keeps styles the game sets borderless. Pass it to `ProtoInput.InstallHook` or `ProtoInput.UninstallHook`.
ProtoInput.Values.RemoveBorderHookID.basis: Nucleus ProtoInput.cs (ExposedValues, ProtoHookIDs), ProtoInputHooks RemoveBorderHook.cpp (RemoveWindowBorder, WaitForWindowBorder, InstallImpl)

ProtoInput.Values.GetCursorInfoID.doc: Meant to select the GetCursorInfo hook, which makes `GetCursorInfo` report the fake cursor position. In Nucleus this value equals `RemoveBorderHookID` (21), so installing it installs the remove border hook instead. Pass it to `ProtoInput.InstallHook` or `ProtoInput.UninstallHook`.
ProtoInput.Values.GetCursorInfoID.basis: Nucleus ProtoInput.cs (ExposedValues, ProtoHookIDs), ProtoInputHooks GetCursorInfoHook.cpp, HookManager.cpp (GetCursorInfoHookID = 22)

ProtoInput.Values.SetWindowsHookHookID.doc: Selects the SetWindowsHook hook (ID 23): the game's low-level keyboard, low-level mouse and `GetMessage` hooks are not registered with Windows; Proto Input calls them itself with the instance's input and focus messages. Pass it to `ProtoInput.InstallHook` or `ProtoInput.UninstallHook`.
ProtoInput.Values.SetWindowsHookHookID.basis: Nucleus ProtoInput.cs (ExposedValues, ProtoHookIDs), ProtoInputHooks SetWindowsHookHook.cpp, FakeMouseKeyboard.cpp, FocusMessageLoop.cpp, RawInput.cpp (FireFake...)
